## Goal

Establish the shared test/verification foundation for the visual storyline
editor so every later feature can be driven test-first. This task writes
**test infrastructure only** — no editor feature code.

## Context

The editor is a dev tool launched under Vite/`vite-node`; the card model
imports `src/card-data.csv` through Vite's `?raw` query, so bridge tests must
run through the same toolchain. Repo test facts:

- `npm test` runs `vitest run --project unit` (Vitest; `tests/**/*.test.ts`,
  excluding `*.browser.test.ts`).
- Browser tests (`tests/**/*.browser.test.ts`) run through Vitest browser mode
  with the Playwright chromium provider (`@vitest/browser`, `playwright` are
  existing devDependencies) — project wiring lives with the launcher
  distribution, so a dev page (not a Phaser scene) needs explicit wiring.
- `ajv` is an existing devDependency and is used for JSON schema validation.
- The root `vite.config.ts` is **auto-generated** by
  `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`; do not hand-edit it — use a dedicated
  editor config file.

## Scope

- Fixture helper that copies `src/card-data.csv`,
  `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` and
  `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` into an isolated temp directory and
  returns the paths, so edit tests never mutate committed files.
- A reusable write-path guard helper: scans editor source files and asserts no
  module writes `src/card-data.csv` except through `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts`
  (tolerant of editor modules not existing yet).
- A manifest schema guard test: committed manifest validates against
  `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` using `ajv`.
- A browser-test harness decision/spike: determine and wire how the editor dev
  page is driven in Vitest browser mode (or justify an alternative), with a
  placeholder test that passes. Record the decision in a comment on this item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture helper returns isolated temp copies of the CSV/manifest/mmd, and a
  test asserts the committed originals are byte-identical afterwards.
- The write-path guard helper is exercised by a test and would fail if an
  editor module wrote the CSV directly (proven with a synthetic negative case).
- The committed manifest validates against the JSON schema in a unit test using
  the existing `ajv` devDependency.
- The browser-test path for a non-Phaser dev page is decided, wired and
  documented; a placeholder browser test passes without adding a runtime
  dependency.
- `npm test` and the browser suite run the new harness green.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/fixtures.ts` — **new** temp-copy helper.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/fixtures.test.ts` — **new** helper test.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/write-path-guard.ts` — **new** reusable static guard.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/write-path-guard.test.ts` — **new**.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/manifest-schema.test.ts` — **new** ajv guard.
- `vite.editor.config.ts` — **new** dedicated editor/harness config (not the auto-generated `./vite.config.ts`).

## Deliverables

- Fixture helper, write-path guard helper, schema guard test, decided + wired
  browser-test path, harness smoke coverage.

# Executive should grant an action point and a single hand slot

The Executive staff card (`staff-executive`) should be repurposed from a pure hand-capacity card into an action-economy card: while employed it grants **+1 action per week** and **+1 hand slot**. This extends the `actionsPerTurn` staff mechanic (introduced by MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0) to the tier-10 Executive and reduces its `handSlotsAdded` from `4` to `1`.

## Problem statement

The Executive is the tier-10 premium capacity card (`handSlotsAdded: 4`, cost 2000, ongoing 500) with no ability. Players who want a top-tier action-economy staff choice currently have only the tier-12 General Manager, so the Executive is a dead-end on the action-economy build axis. Granting the Executive `actionsPerTurn: 1` — traded against dropping its hand-slot bonus to a single slot — gives it a distinct, legible role.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — wants a tier-10 action-economy staff option before the tier-12 General Manager is affordable.
- **Main Street player (mid/late game)** — wants the Executive's role to be clear: a tempo (extra action) card rather than a bulk hand-capacity card.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want to hire an Executive that grants +1 action per week and +1 hand slot so that I can take an extra action each week without waiting for the General Manager.
- As a Main Street player, I want the Executive's card art, tooltip and description to state the +1 action/week and the single hand slot so that I understand what I am buying.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `src/card-data.csv` `staff-executive` row sets `actionsPerTurn` to `1` and `handSlotsAdded` to `1` (down from `4`), keeping `cost: 2000`, `ongoingCost: 500`, tier `10`, and the generalist `allowedBusinessTypes` (`Food|Culture|Service|Commerce|Entertainment|Health`); the CSV `description` states the `+1` hand slot and the `+1` action/week (and no longer claims "major hand capacity" / `+4` slots). CSV column order is unchanged.
- **AC2** — The parsed `StaffCard` template for `staff-executive` exposes `actionsPerTurn === 1` and `handSlotsAdded === 1`, and `executeWeekStart` composes the weekly budget as `1 base + sum(actionsPerTurn) + banked (capped at 2)` with the Executive included, preserving the existing invariants (staff actions consumed first, never banked; bank cap 2).
- **AC3** — The staff card formatting and Actions HUD tooltip render the Executive's `Actions: +1/week` benefit and the in-game Help panel "Turn Flow" text lists the Executive among action-granting staff (Manager, Director, Executive, General Manager).
- **AC4** — The committed card art `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/staff-executive.svg` is regenerated to show `+1 slots` (not `+4 slots`), and `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` matches the new `src/card-data.csv` content.
- **AC5** — Tests assert the new Executive contract and no-regression for staff without the ability: `tests/main-street/action-economy.test.ts` (Executive grants +1 action/turn and +1 slot; only Manager, Director, Executive and General Manager grant `actionsPerTurn`), `tests/main-street/group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` (the Executive design-contract entry and the non-ability block are updated so the Executive is no longer listed as ability-free), and existing action-budget/tooltip tests remain green.
- **AC6** — Documentation is updated to reflect the change: `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (§ 6.0 action-economy staff list), `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` (staff table), `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (staff catalogue row + rationale), and `docs/main-street/prd-multi-use-card-economy.md` (staff template table).
- **AC7** — All related documentation and user-facing text (code comments/doc-strings, `README.md` where it references the affected card or the action list, in-game help panel) is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- **AC8** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Mechanic already exists** — reuse `actionsPerTurn` (CSV column, `StaffCard.actionsPerTurn`, `executeWeekStart`, tooltip/formatting). No new engine mechanic, schema column, or save-format change is expected; the change is data + card art + docs + test coverage.
- Preserve the existing action-economy invariants: bank cap of 2, base-only banking, staff actions consumed first and never banked, and the defensive clamp in `executeWeekStart`.
- CSV column order must remain unchanged (edit in place); `actionsPerTurn` is already a known column.
- Do not alter the Manager, Director or General Manager as part of this item.
- Card SVG generation is driven by the CSV + `csv-checksum.json`; the committed SVG must be regenerated with the project generator (`node src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) rather than hand-edited.

## Existing state

- `src/card-data.csv`: `staff-executive` = `handSlotsAdded 4`, no `actionsPerTurn`, `cost 2000`, `ongoingCost 500`, tier 10, description "An experienced executive adds major hand capacity at a high ongoing cost."
- Action-granting staff today (MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0): Manager (tier 3, 700/250, +1 slot, +1 action), Director (tier 9, 1400/400, +3 slots, +1 action), General Manager (tier 12, 2000/500, +4 slots, +1 action). The Executive, Apprentice, Socialite, Accountant, Lookout, Investor and the specialization applicants do not grant actions.
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` (`executeWeekStart`): budget = `1 + sum(staff.actionsPerTurn ?? 0) + min(2, bankedActions)` — logic is already generic.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` (staff case): renders `Actions: +N/week` when `actionsPerTurn > 0`; `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` (`buildActionTooltip`) appends the generic action-granting-staff note when any employed staff has `actionsPerTurn > 0`.
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` "Turn Flow" body lists "(Manager, Director, General Manager)".
- Card art `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/staff-executive.svg` currently renders `+4 slots`; `csv-checksum.json` is committed alongside.
- Tests today: `tests/main-street/action-economy.test.ts` (asserts the ladder and "only Manager, Director and General Manager grant `actionsPerTurn`"), `tests/main-street/group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` (Executive contract `handSlotsAdded: 4`; Executive in the "staff without the ability" block), `tests/main-street/hud-tooltips.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/staff-business-type-matching.test.ts` (Executive generalist — should remain unchanged).

## Desired change

- CSV: `staff-executive` → `actionsPerTurn 1`, `handSlotsAdded 1`, description updated to state the `+1` hand slot and `+1` action/week.
- Card art: regenerate `staff-executive.svg` and `csv-checksum.json`.
- Help/tooltip text: add the Executive to the "Turn Flow" action-granting-staff list (`src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts`); confirm `MainStreetFormatting`/`MainStreetHudTooltips` need no logic change.
- Docs: update the four tables/sections listed in AC6 and the action-economy staff list.
- Tests: assert the Executive's new contract and update the "only these staff grant actions" and "staff without the ability" assertions; add a week-start budget composition case including the Executive.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — `staff-executive` row: `actionsPerTurn 1`, `handSlotsAdded 1`, refreshed `description`.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/staff-executive.svg` — regenerated card art showing `+1 slots`.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` — regenerated checksum matching the new CSV.
- `tests/main-street/action-economy.test.ts` — Executive contract + broaden the action-granting set; add composition case.
- `tests/main-street/group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` — update the Executive design-contract entry and remove it from the "no ability" block.
- `tests/main-street/hud-tooltips.test.ts` — cover the Executive-derived action budget where relevant.
- `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts` — assert the Executive appears in the action-granting-staff list.
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` — add the Executive to the "Turn Flow" staff list.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — refresh the `actionsPerTurn` doc comment if it names only the General Manager.
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` — verify `executeWeekStart` composes the budget with the Executive included; no logic change expected (AC2).
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — verify the existing `Actions: +N/week` rendering needs no logic change (AC3).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — verify the generic action-granting-staff tooltip note needs no logic change (AC3).
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — § 6.0 action-economy staff list.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — staff table row.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — staff catalogue row and rationale.
- `docs/main-street/prd-multi-use-card-economy.md` — staff template table.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Balance dominance (assumption / open question):** with `handSlotsAdded: 1` + `actionsPerTurn: 1` at `2000/500` tier 10, the Executive is strictly dominated by the Director (tier 9, `1400/400`, `+3` slots, `+1` action) and by the General Manager (tier 12, `2000/500`, `+4` slots, `+1` action). **Assumption:** the operator intends the literal `+1` slot / `+1` action, and tier-gating (Executive unlocks before the General Manager) is the intended differentiator; any cost/tier rebalance is out of scope for this item. See the Appendix open question.
- **Scope-creep risk:** regenerating SVGs touches only the Executive's card content, but the checksum file changes for the whole CSV; treat that as a generated artefact — do not hand-edit other SVGs.
- **Assumption:** the `actionsPerTurn` engine path is already generic (verified in `executeWeekStart`), so no engine change is required; if a hidden General-Manager-specific assumption surfaces, prefer generalising the comment/text over special-casing.
- **Failure mode:** forgetting to regenerate `csv-checksum.json` would make the runtime regenerate art on load and could break checksum tests — regenerate both together.
- Out of scope: any change to the Manager, Director, General Manager, the bank cap, or the save format; any new card or art beyond regenerating the Executive SVG.

## Related work

- **MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0 — Some staff cards should add action points** (completed): introduced `actionsPerTurn` on the Manager and Director and documented the ladder Assistant → Manager → Director → Executive (+4 slots). This item supersedes that item's AC2 statement that the Executive stays at `+4` slots.
- **MS-0MTISBYLS009936W — Add Investor staff members** (completed): precedent for adding a staff ability (`freeMarketRerollPerTurn`) via CSV + types + docs + tests.
- **CG-0MSQJ7VL9009JHF4** (Group F staff expansion epic) and **CG-0MSQE2NLX003ADIY**: introduced the Executive as a premium capacity card.
- **CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R**: original General Manager action-economy mechanic.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "The Executive will become `+1` hand slot and `+1` action/week at 2000/500 tier 10. That makes it strictly dominated by the Director (tier 9, 1400/400, +3 slots, +1 action) and the General Manager (tier 12, 2000/500, +4 slots, +1 action). Should the Executive's cost/ongoing/tier also be adjusted, or should the literal `+1` slot / `+1` action be implemented as written and any rebalance handled separately?" — **OPEN QUESTION.** No operator answer recorded during intake. **Agent recommendation (advisory):** implement the literal request now (AC1–AC8) and raise a separate balance work item if the dominance is confirmed as unintended; alternatively reduce the Executive's `cost`/`ongoingCost` (or raise its slots) so it is not strictly worse than the Director.
  - Evidence: `src/card-data.csv` staff rows; `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` staff table; `tests/main-street/action-economy.test.ts` ("only Manager, Director and General Manager grant actionsPerTurn").
- Q: "Does 'a single hand slot' mean `handSlotsAdded` should be `1` (replacing the current `4`)?" — Answer (derived from the work-item description and title, not an interactive reply): yes — the description explicitly says "grant an action point and a single hand slot", and this brief assumes the current `+4` is reduced to `+1`. Source: `wl show MS-0MUYAEXBN008YC0J`.
- Q: "Is a duplicate of an existing item?" — **Duplicate check performed** (`wl search executive|action economy|staff balance|hand slot`): closest match is MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0 (completed), which intentionally left the Executive unchanged. This item is a **partial overlap / extension**, not a duplicate; the brief addresses only the Executive delta. Source: `wl search` results; `wl show MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUMM69OL008ZMK2** – Commit game-repo scaffolding files (.githooks, AGENTS.md, package-lock.json) (open)
- **MS-0MUOSUMNK000QZ62** – Update documentation for Investor card and mechanics (completed)
- **MS-0MV33NV6O002WBYA** – Test: per-seat challenge completion attribution (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: abilities, ability, acceptance, action, actions (+318 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: abilities, ability, acceptance, action, actions (+250 more)
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — matched: 0msqj7vl9009jhf4, 0mstof1n5005pk2r, 0mtisbyls009936w, 0mtq7s5ej008mwd0, ability (+245 more)

# Intake Brief — Spread tier reputation thresholds and cap tier unlocks to one per game

Work item: **MS-0MV88T4I6000HQZG** — "Spread tier reputation thresholds per Monte Carlo ranges and cap tier unlocks to one per game" (`feature`, priority `high`)

## Headline

Tier unlocks by reputation currently fire in bursts (a median Medium run clears the 400/800/1200/1600 rungs in one go), so the ladder reveals content without pacing. Re-derive the 12-tier reputation thresholds from the Monte-Carlo-measured reputation distribution (Medium, achievement-rate steps) and cap progression at **one tier unlock per run**.

## Problem statement

Reputation thresholds for the early tiers (T2–T5 = 400/800/1200/1600) sit far below typical end-of-run reputation: a median Medium run ends around 2,900 rep, so `updateCampaignAfterRun` unlocks **4–6 tiers in a single run** (400, 800, 1200, 1600, 2400 are all cleared, adding the challenge triggers). Multiple new card families appear at once, there is no sense of a hard-won milestone, and the remaining ladder (up to T12 = 8000) is far out of reach — an unsatisfying pacing cliff at both ends.

## Users

Main Street players engaging with the campaign meta-progression (unlock ladder). The reputation path is the primary unlock driver; the challenge path is an alternative trigger per PRD M2.

Example user stories:
- "As a returning player, I want each run to unlock at most one new tier so that unlocking a tier feels like a milestone rather than a content dump."
- "As a player climbing the ladder, I want thresholds spaced so that consecutive unlocks are genuinely earned across several runs."
- "As a challenge-focused player, I still want the challenge path to unlock tiers, but it must obey the same one-per-run pacing."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Threshold spread (reputation path).** The 12-tier reputation thresholds are re-derived from a **fresh Medium Monte-Carlo run on current HEAD** (≥ 200 seeds, greedy strategy via `src/scripts/monte-carlo.ts`, `economyHistory` final reputation) to hit the target achievement shares — the % of Medium runs whose end-of-run reputation clears the tier: **T2 90%, T3 75%, T4 60%, T5 45%, T6 35%, T7 25%, T8 18%, T9 12%, T10 8%, T11 4%, T12 1%**. The derived thresholds are recorded with the MC evidence (percentile table, run counts). Exact values may be rounded to friendly numbers and document that rounding; monotonic increasing order is preserved. (Existing `results/level2-gate-before-*.json` are treated as stale — generated 2026-10-07, before later balance changes; a fresh run is required.)
2. **T12 / top tiers stay aspirational.** No threshold is artificially compressed into the observed rep range; T12 (and the top tiers) may sit above the observed maximum and remain primarily challenge-path / long-campaign reachable.
3. **One tier unlock per run.** `updateCampaignAfterRun` (in `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts`) unlocks **at most one** tier per completed run: the **lowest newly-eligible locked tier** (no skipping), regardless of whether eligibility came from the reputation path, the challenge path, or both.
4. **Challenge path preserved but capped.** All challenge-based unlock conditions remain unchanged and still work as an alternative trigger; the one-per-run cap applies to them identically.
5. **UI consistency.** Any surface showing a tier threshold or next-tier target (e.g. `findNextLockedTier`/`scoreNextTierLabel` in `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`) reflects the new thresholds; no stale hard-coded figures remain in i18n/UI text.
6. **Tests.** `tests/main-street/meta-progression.test.ts` is updated: the existing "unlocks multiple tiers in a single high-reputation run" case becomes an assertion that exactly one (lowest) tier unlocks; new cases cover cap semantics (rep-only, challenge-only, both-triggers, next-run continuation, already-unlocked tiers, T12 aspirational). All existing tier/progression/save-load tests continue to pass.
7. **Evidence + docs.** The Monte-Carlo reputation-distribution evidence and the new threshold table are committed, and the relevant docs are updated: `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` (US-1/update notes + threshold calibration appendix), plus `content-design-and-progression.md` if it restates thresholds. CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** (ship skill manages it).
8. **Full project test suite passes** with the change (unit + unit-cli + smoke, per the test skill).

## Constraints

- **Calibration basis (Q2-A):** thresholds are calibrated on **Medium** difficulty only. Easy runs will generally unlock faster and Hard runs slower — accepted drift documented in the brief/PRD (one ladder cannot pace all three economies equally).
- **No skipping (Q1-A):** the one-per-run cap always unlocks the **lowest** newly-eligible locked tier; the ladder is never jumped.
- **Achievement-rate steps (Q3-B):** thresholds are not evenly spaced; they are placed to hit the pre-defined share steps above. Where the Medium distribution is clumpy (a 5% band between ~794 and ~2152 yields a large threshold gap; the ≥2000–4500 mass yields tight mid-ladder gaps), the shares are authoritative and thresholds follow the data.
- **Challenge conditions unchanged** — out of scope to redesign; only their interaction with the cap changes.
- `campaign.unlockedTiers` / `milestoneHistory` schema and save/load format unchanged (only the number of tiers appended per run changes).

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetTiers.ts` — `TIER_CONFIG` holds the 12 thresholds: 0, 400, 800, 1200, 1600, 2400, 3200, 4000, 4800, 5600, 6400, 8000; card-to-tier mapping lives in `src/card-data.csv` (out of scope here).
- `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` `updateCampaignAfterRun` — iterates all locked tiers; `if (reputationMet || challengeMet) campaign.unlockedTiers.push(...)` → multi-unlock per run.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — `findNextLockedTier` shows `requires Rep ≥ <threshold>`.
- `tests/main-street/meta-progression.test.ts` — US-1 tests pin old thresholds (400→T2, etc.) and explicitly pin "unlocks multiple tiers in a single high-reputation run".
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` §2/§8 (US-1) and Appendix B — PRD originally specified multi-tier unlock and 5-tier thresholds; expanded to 12 tiers (CG-0MT3C744B009DS84).
- Existing MC evidence: `results/level2-gate-before-greedy-{easy,medium,hard}.json` (200 runs each, 2026-10-07). Medium: mean 2632, median 2896, p10 132, p25 794, p50 2900, p75 3752, p90 4712, max 6272.
- MC harness records per-turn `economyHistory` (incl. reputation) but **not** `challengesCompleted` per run — challenge-path shares are measured separately or estimated during implementation; the share table above is reputation-path.

## Desired change

1. Run a fresh Medium MC calibration pass on HEAD; extract the final-reputation distribution.
2. Compute thresholds from the share table (percentile lookup), round sensibly, keep monotonic.
3. Update `TIER_CONFIG` thresholds.
4. Add the one-per-run cap (lowest eligible) to `updateCampaignAfterRun`.
5. Update the HUD-tier tooltip plumbing only if the new thresholds flow through configuration (no hard-coded UI strings).
6. Update tests + PRD/evidence docs.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetTiers.ts` — `TIER_CONFIG.reputationThreshold` values (primary change).
- `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — `updateCampaignAfterRun` one-per-run cap (primary change).
- `src/scripts/monte-carlo.ts` / `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — fresh calibration evidence; note the harness currently omits per-run `challengesCompleted` (add if needed for challenge-path evidence).
- `results/main-street-monte-carlo*.json` — committed calibration evidence artifacts.
- `tests/main-street/meta-progression.test.ts` — cap + threshold tests.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — verify next-tier threshold display uses `TIER_DEFINITIONS` (update if any stale constants remain).
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — US-1/update notes, threshold calibration appendix.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — threshold restatements if any.
- `docs/dev/` / `CHANGELOG.md` — CHANGELOG excluded; no docs/dev change expected.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Clumpy MC distribution:** the Medium rep distribution is bimodal (a low cluster ~0–800 that includes collapsed/bankrupt runs and a dense 2000–4500 body). Percentile-derived mid-ladder thresholds will be close together (hundreds apart) on the dense body; the one-per-run cap is what prevents burst unlocks there, and the share steps are authoritative — exact value selection must be documented so the "too close together" complaint does not silently return.
- **Stale calibration source:** existing `results/` MC files predate later balance changes; thresholds are only finalised against a fresh run on HEAD. If the fresh distribution differs materially, the share table survives and threshold *values* follow the new percentiles (replan, do not fudge).
- **Challenge-path shares unknown:** the MC harness does not record per-run `challengesCompleted`; the share table above is reputation-path only. Adding challenge-path evidence is a possible small harness scope increase (note in plan, do not silently expand).
- **Save/load & schema:** only the number of tiers appended per run changes; `milestoneHistory` entries remain per-unlock (one per qualifying run). Existing saves with already-unlocked tiers must not regress (multi-tier saves keep their tiers).
- **UI text:** thresholds appear in HUD tooltip text — any hard-coded numbers must flow from `TIER_DEFINITIONS`; flag dead constants rather than silently updating strings in isolation.
- **Scope-creep guard:** redesigning challenge conditions, rebalancing rep sources, or adjusting card-to-tier assignments are explicitly out of scope; record such opportunities as linked work items, not gold-plating here.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE** (completed, high) — "Re-tune reputation sources…": ×4 retune of rep sources directly inflates the rep scale and makes the pre-retune thresholds (and any pre-retune calibration) stale.
- **MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4** (completed) — Level-2 gate MC evidence (`results/level2-gate-*.json`): source of the current (stale) reputation distribution.
- **MS-0MUQUBK1B006EODZ / MS-0MUQUBJ4J000IQT7** (completed) — Monte-Carlo baseline and evidence methodology this calibration extends.
- **MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M** (completed) — 5-turn payback rebalance; relevant economy vector.
- **MS-0MUYGFVIJ00070MB** (completed) — Reputation-phase invariant regression tests (guard against rep-path regressions while touching thresholds).
- Docs: `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` (M2 tier ladder, US-1, Appendix B), `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md`, `docs/main-street/reputation-retune-evidence.md`.

## Appendix — Clarifying questions & answers (interview round)

- Q1 (round 1): "When a run would newly qualify for several locked tiers, which one unlocks?" — **Answer (operator): A — lowest newly-eligible tier (no skipping).** Source: interactive reply. Recommended option A chosen.
- Q2 (round 1): "Which difficulty should the threshold spread be calibrated to?" — **Answer (operator): A — Medium only** (Easy faster, Hard slower, accepted drift). Source: interactive reply. Recommended option A chosen.
- Q3 (round 1): "Preferred spread shape: evenly across p10–p90, or clustered to pre-defined achievement-rate steps?" — **Answer (operator): B — achievement-rate steps** (e.g. T2 by 80%, T3 by 50%…). Source: interactive reply. Recommended option A, operator overrode to B — brief follows B.
- Q4 (round 2): "Confirm the achievement-rate staircase (T2 90% … T12 1%)?" — **Answer (operator): "3. ?" — no preference / delegated to agent; proceeding with the recommended staircase** (90/75/60/45/35/25/18/12/8/4/1). Source: interactive reply ("?"). Interpretation recorded; revisit if the operator intended otherwise.
- Q5 (round 2): "May the top tiers (notably T12) stay aspirational above the observed rep max?" — **Answer (operator): "4. confirm / A" — yes, aspirational (option A)**. Source: interactive reply.

Research note: existing `results/` MC files predate later balance changes (running-costs etc.), so the brief requires a fresh calibration run; thresholds are targets, not final numbers, until that run lands. MC harness omits per-run challenge completion data — challenge-path share evidence may require a small harness addition (scoped at plan time).

data.description:
# Piggyback eligibility flag and card data (F1)

## Target outcome
Add a per-card opt-in `piggybackable` flag to Investment event cards so only "organiser" events trigger the piggyback mechanic (epic MS-0MUYC47EL005Z69H; producer Q1: organiser events only — festivals, fairs, community gatherings).

## Context
- Applies in competitive mode (N≥2) only. The flag is per-card; engine behaviour is built in F2/F3.
- Per-plan decision (2026-10-14 Q1, producer answer "A"): flag exactly the 16 town-wide festival/fair/party/celebration cards.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** `src/card-data.csv` gains a `piggybackable` column and `EventCard` gains `readonly piggybackable?: boolean`; absent values parse to falsy/absent (backwards compatible, older saves unaffected).
- [ ] **AC2** Exactly the 16 Option-A cards are flagged `true`: Local Festival, Wellness Fair, Block Party, Harvest Festival, Book Fair, Garden Party, Festival Season, Health Carnival, Summer Fest, St Brigid's Day, St Patrick's Day, Easter, May Day/Bealtaine, Lughnasadh, Samhain/Halloween, Christmas. No other row is flagged.
- [ ] **AC3** Unit tests assert the flagged set and that non-organiser events (e.g. Grand Opening Sale, Charity Drive, Bulk Purchase, Volunteer Day) have `piggybackable` falsy.
- [ ] **AC4** Card catalog docs (if regenerated) and CsvChecksum reflect the new column; no unrelated card data changes.

- [ ] **Satisfies epic AC1** — - [ ] **AC1 — Eligibility & trigger.** When an active player plays a piggyback-eligible **organiser** Investment event during their MarketPhase in competitive mode (N≥2), every other non-eliminated player automatically receives the 50% free-ride share and is offered the join-fully upgrade for that event; playing a non-eligible event (or any event in N=1) produces no share and no prompt. Verified by unit tests over a flagged eligible card and an unflagged card.

## Minimal implementation
- Add `piggybackable` CSV column + `true` on the 16 rows; new column header.
- Add `piggybackable?: boolean` to `EventCard` in `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`.
- Parse the flag in `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` next to `hasChoices` (spread only when true, keeping older templates unchanged).
- New unit test file asserting the expected flagged IDs and a falsy default.

## Key Files
- src/card-data.csv
- src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts
- src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts
- tests/main-street/piggyback-eligibility.test.ts (new)

## Dependencies
- None (foundational).

## Deliverables
CSV data + `EventCard.piggybackable` + parser + eligibility unit tests.
data.title: Piggyback eligibility flag + organiser card data
